$comment: The Portage demo video. Each segment is a title card or a scene. Narration is a list of lines and pauses (seconds); a scene lasts its narration plus 0.6 s. Actions run on camera; `at` is seconds from the scene start or `pN[+s]` (the start of narration line N, counting lines only). `setup` runs off camera before the scene starts. Numbers in the narration are the ones on screen at that moment.

segments.title: Why Portage
narration: Canada's biggest untapped resource isn't in the ground.

Meet Priya. She was an ICU nurse for eight years. In Waterloo, she works retail. Priya is a composite of many real stories, and Canada needs nurses like her. She has the skills. What she does not have is a clear path to her licence.
To practise in Ontario, she has to meet nine separate requirements, across several organizations.
The college's own guideline is about twelve months, and seven thousand, nine hundred and fifty-seven internationally educated applicants are waiting in Ontario right now.
People lose months to steps done in the wrong order, and to documents that expire.

card.line: Tell us your story in your own language.

segments.title: Sign in and profile
narration: Portage turns that maze into one personal plan, with the official source for every step, and the deadlines that can quietly reset months of progress.
Priya signs in with the demo account. It lives only in this browser.
Her profile holds everything Portage knows: what she said in her voice interview, and what her documents show. Every fact says where it came from, and she can edit any of it.
Her employment letter says Priya Anand Deshpande, but she said Priya Deshpande. Portage never overwrites her silently. She picks her passport name, and the document check will use it.

segments.title: Guided voice interview
narration: Most people don't know what to say. So Portage asks one question at a time, in their own language, with an example, and anything can be skipped.
Here is question three, read aloud in Hindi.
Her six answers become one transcript. The AI only reads it and pulls out the facts. It never invents a requirement.
Then she checks every fact, and it all lands on her profile.

card.line: Every requirement, in the right order, with the official source.

segments.title: The roadmap
narration: The roadmap shows every CNO requirement, in order, each with its official source.
One step at a time, Priya's earliest licence is December 2027. Her evidence of practice window closes in July 2027, before she finishes, so she would have to start over.
The same steps, done in parallel, are the Portage plan. Her earliest licence moves to April 2027.
It is tight, so Portage shows exactly what protects her window, starting now. Every duration is labelled official or estimate, and the date only holds if each step goes to plan.
Each step shows who does it, how long it takes, and a link to the regulator's own page.
And she can hear her plan in Hindi.

target.text: Your evidence of practice may expire

card.line: Catch document problems before they cost you months.

segments.title: Document check
narration: Before she mails anything, Portage checks it. Here is her police check.
CNO only accepts police checks through its approved provider. And this one is too early: it would expire before she registers.
These findings come from CNO's rules, not from the AI. Some documents must come directly from an employer or a school, and Portage catches that too. Every result is saved to her profile.

segments.title: Insights for government
narration: For governments and regulators, Portage shows where Canada's talent gets stuck.
Seven thousand, nine hundred and fifty-seven international applicants are waiting in Ontario. Six thousand, seven hundred and thirty-eight nurses have registered after supervised practice.
Ontario is live, and every new province is a new data file plus expert review. The stage funnel is illustrative, and it says so.
This is the view the ministers' platform needs: where applicants stall, requirement by requirement.

segments.title: Why now
narration: Why now? In July 2026, Canada's labour ministers agreed to build a digital platform for credential recognition. We built the prototype this weekend.
Portage is free for newcomers, always. Regulators, employers and settlement agencies pay.
Checklists are generic, and general AI guesses. Portage gives each person a cited, deadline-aware plan, and gives government a live view of where people get stuck.
Next: five interviews with internationally educated nurses, one pilot conversation with a settlement agency, then engineers, a skilled trade, and a second province.
